bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical tensions and supply chain disruptions — Escalating conflicts, particularly in West Asia, disrupt critical global shipping routes and add upward pressure on energy and raw material costs, impacting manufacturing and input costs.
- Commodity price inflation — Prolonged geopolitical conflicts in the Middle East pose a risk of commodity inflation, which could pressure margins.
- Climate transition risk from inadequate clean technology investment — Failure to invest in low-carbon technologies may increase operational carbon footprint, constrain ability to meet emissions reduction and net zero commitments, and heighten exposure to changing customer preferences and regulatory expectations.
- Water stress and stewardship — Water is a critical input for manufacturing; inadequate water stewardship in water-stressed regions could lead to inefficient use, increased pressure on local resources, and operational/reputational risks.
- Regulatory and compliance risk from evolving wage codes — The impact of the New Wage Code, 2019 increased manpower costs, indicating exposure to evolving labour regulations.
- Customer concentration risk — The company caters to major Tier 1 & Tier 2 segments, two & three-wheeler companies, passenger vehicle manufacturers, Indian Railways, and commercial vehicle manufacturers, implying potential concentration risk if key OEM relationships are disrupted.

outlook.body:
- The Company has a Dividend Distribution Policy approved by the Board. It declared an interim dividend and recommended a final dividend, reflecting a consistent shareholder return philosophy. No share buyback or bonus issue occurred during the year.
- Targeting 60% domestic value addition in premium components through localization programs.
- Developing advanced light weighting technologies to support OEMs in meeting upcoming CAFE 3 emissions norms.
- Integrating climate considerations into capital expenditure and procurement decisions by evaluating carbon footprint of new machinery and prioritizing energy-efficient and low-emission technologies.
- Emphasizing sourcing and use of renewable and green energy to reduce Scope 2 emissions.
- Implementing a structured water stewardship program with specific water reduction targets, closed-loop systems, reuse and recycling mechanisms, and regular monitoring of water withdrawal and efficiency metrics.
- Adopting systematic waste reduction, reuse, and recycling practices across manufacturing operations to enhance resource efficiency.
- Prioritizing adoption of energy-optimized technologies, modern equipment, and efficient operational practices to lower energy demand and reduce Scope 1 emissions.

outlook.body: During FY 2025-26, Gabriel India advanced a major corporate restructuring through a Composite Scheme of Arrangement, which became effective on May 22, 2026. The Scheme involved the merger of Anchemco India Private Limited (a fellow subsidiary engaged in brake fluids, coolants, DEF/ad-blue, and adhesives) into Asia Investments Private Limited (the immediate holding company), followed by the demerger of the Automotive Undertaking of AIPL into Gabriel India. This reorganisation transforms the Company from a monoproduct suspension-focused entity into a diversified mobility solutions provider with an expanded presence across automotive components, EV products, fluids, and industrial solutions. The restructuring is expected to streamline the corporate structure, eliminate intragroup transactions, unlock operational synergies, and enable more effective capital allocation. No specific new plant, line, or capacity expansion projects with timelines were disclosed.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
